title: HDB resale price moderation and support for first-time buyers
asked: Mr Victor Lye asked whether the recent moderation in HDB resale prices is broad-based across flat types and towns or concentrated in selected segments, and what additional measures the Ministry is considering for first-time buyers who still cannot secure affordable housing near their parents or workplaces.
response: Mr Chee Hong Tat said HDB resale prices declined by 0.1% in the first quarter of 2026, after five consecutive quarters of moderating price growth, and that the moderation is broad-based across flat types and towns. He listed measures already in place for first-time buyers: more Plus and Prime flats with additional subsidies, the Family Care Scheme introduced in 2025, and enhanced grants of up to $120,000 for new flats and $230,000 for resale flats, with a Proximity Housing Grant of up to $30,000 for resale buyers. On the supplementary, he pointed to HDB's published application rates, said the February BTO exercise showed improved first-timer application rates with some projects below one, and said 2-room Flexi flat supply will increase by about 50% from 2026 to 2028.

left_open: Whether any additional measures beyond those already implemented are being considered for first-time buyers who cannot secure housing near their parents or workplaces
Whether more granular, area-specific data can be provided to guide buyers between the resale route and the BTO route
Whether the Ministry has studied how the ageing population and right-sizing could affect supply and resale prices in mature estates
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered more granular application-rate data for choosing between resale and BTO flats, and seniors right-sizing and its effect on supply.
